ev.q: In 2021, 64.8% of adults aged ≥18 years took prescription medication at any time during the past 12 months.
The percentage of adults taking prescription medication was lower among men than women overall (58.4% versus 70.9%)
In 2021, 64.8% of adults aged ≥18 years took prescription medication at any time during the past 12 months.
The percentage of adults taking prescription medication was lower among men than women overall (58.4% versus 70.9%)
and for those aged 18–44 years (38.9% versus 57.8%) and 45–64 years (67.1% versus 75.7%).
Among adults aged ≥65 years, men (89.0%) and women (89.3%) were equally likely to take prescription medication.
Prescription medication use increased with age, from 48.4% for those aged 18–44 years to 89.2% for those aged ≥65 years

notes: Survey weighting is not stated, so it is not recorded as a procedure. The sex contrast is reported within age groups, which is read as stratified.
view_issues: Claims such as 'lower' and 'equally likely' are made without any stated testing method. Only 95% CIs of the separate estimates are shown, as error bars.
